correctness.rationale: Even terms require odd digit sums of their base-b quotients. Adding one without changing digit-sum parity requires an odd number of trailing b−1 digits, so the next quotient ends in zero and the following increment flips parity. With b≥6, successive even progression terms are spaced six apart and their quotients cannot skip a block. Hence they occupy at most two adjacent blocks, containing at most ceil(b/3) such even terms, proving the stated bound. For the listed seeds the carry in the low digit starts at one at j=1, runs through two, and reaches three only at the last term, with final remainder one. Subtraction of the digit sum gives (b−1) times U, U+2 and U+3 on these three cases. The factor b−1=3^k is harmless because every term is K modulo 3. Independently parsed the twelve rows from RESULT.md, checked the two endpoint gcds and prime-factor tests by trial division, and checked all 1,594,356 terms with exact gcd and base-b digit sums. The largest row has 1,062,885 terms. The low block stays below b^3 throughout; a common multiple of the multiplicative orders for primes dividing the finitely many digit sums and not dividing b preserves all relevant residues when shifting the leading one to b^m. Primes dividing b see both powers as zero. Arbitrarily large m preserve all gcds and give distinct starts.
residual_risks: Only twelve bases are certified attainments. The computation establishes witness terms and certificate conditions, not the universal bound or infinitude, which follow from the separate arguments.

value.rationale: The stride and base family are motivated by the even-base extremal problem and the identity b−1=3^k, which isolates one forced carry prime. This is a meaningful finite cutoff: the same small certificate shape works for twelve exponentially growing bases, including a maximal progression of over one million terms. The extension from a seed to infinitely many maximal starts shows more than existence of isolated computer hits.
residual_risks: No assertion of sharpness beyond k=13 or enumeration of all maximizing starts; the certificate search does not prove such seeds must continue to exist.
